evidence: Every public promise that is interactive, time-varying or viewport-dependent has a criterion or prompt step that tells the judge to act, wait or resize; none is scored from a still first paint. (1) Viewport: environment/instructions/ui.md:17 'At a phone width of about 390 px the editor and its controls, the preview, the console and the library must all stay usable without sideways page scrolling' is exercised by polish cw_narrow_width_usable: 'Resize the browser viewport to about 390 by 844 pixels and reload ... By scrolling only vertically, reach the code editor, the Run control, the preview, the console and the library. At this width type a short line in the editor and see it appear, and press the Run control ... Restore the desktop viewport afterwards.' The visual prompt (scored/visual/prompt.md:13) says 'First resize the browser to a desktop viewport of about 1440 by 900 pixels', so its scores do not depend on whatever viewport is left over. (2) Time-varying: functional prompt.md:27 'Where waiting is required, wait the stated time; do not shorten it'; stated waits are present wherever the product promise is about time: cw_multi_caret_typing_atomic 'wait about three seconds without any other input' (ui.md burst 'however slowly'), cw_interaction_starts_fresh_budget 'wait at least eight more seconds so the original five seconds have long passed', cw_time_limit_recovery 'within about ten seconds a visible time-limit reason must appear', cw_stop_cancels_pending_work and cw_newer_run_supersedes 'wait at least eight more seconds' after a working control proved the delayed write really happens, cw_live_library_update 'watch its library for up to ten seconds ... without reloading or pressing anything in A', cw_newer_revision_notice_keeps_draft 'Wait ten seconds and confirm that A shows no notice ... yet: this is the baseline'. Racy steps carry a void-and-repeat rule instead of a one-second distinction. (3) Interaction: all 43 functional and 6 polish criteria prescribe real keys, mouse, drags, modifier-clicks and scrolling (cw_caret_kept_in_view, cw_long_line_editing make the editor scroll); focus visibility is checked while tabbing (cw_controls_keyboard_and_focus), disabled/enabled and unsaved-marker state changes are checked across actions (cw_undo_redo_availability, cw_unsaved_marker). The render gate types and reloads; the constraints gate types, saves, clears storage and reloads. (4) Animation: the only animated element a criterion grades is the caret; visual prompt.md:14 'click once into the code and watch the caret for about two seconds, because a caret may blink, and take one screenshot that shows it', then a double-click selection for the remaining screenshots, which matches cw_visual_editor_readability ('visibility of the caret and of a selection'). (5) Themed: no public note asks for themes and no criterion grades one, so no toggle is owed. Weak-app test: a desktop-only layout that overflows at 390 px fails cw_narrow_width_usable; an app whose Stop only hides output and lets the timer fire later fails after the eight-second wait; a library that refreshes only on reload fails cw_live_library_update; a burst-by-idle-timeout undo fails the three-second pause. Conforming-alternative test: a canvas editor, a 5 s polling library, a blinking caret and native confirm dialogs are all tolerated by app_context.md notes. Run evidence: scripted golden on these bytes passes all 3 gate, 43 functional and 6 polish checks including a real 390x844 resize (tests/polish.cjs:111, results/polish.json cw_narrow_width_usable true); this is scripted evidence, not a judge run. The hosted configured judge on the EARLIER candidate did resize and wait (reasoning: 'Viewport resized to 390x844 and reloaded: ... scrollWidth 390 = clientWidth 390'; 'appear in A's library within ~6s without reload or any input in A'), which shows the tools can do this, not that these bytes were judged. NOTES (not defects): (a) cw_narrow_width_usable only requires the preview, console and library to be reached at 390 px and Run to be pressable; it does not ask the judge to read output in the narrow preview/console or open a library entry there, so 'stay usable' is exercised for the editor and Run and only by visibility for the other three areas. (b) behaviour.md:16 promises the library updates 'within about five seconds'; the criteria allow ten, a lenient margin that favours conforming apps. (c) cw_live_update_keeps_editing_state says 'wait until A's library shows it' with no bound; the ten-second bound lives in the sibling criterion. (d) The visual dimension is desktop-only by design ('Do not score ... narrow-screen behavior here'), unlike the template's 390 px visual step; narrow layout is covered once, in polish, and no visual criterion claims responsiveness. (e) No configured judge run exists for these exact bytes; whether GLM actually performs each wait is unmeasured here.
